title: Royal Caribbean Wants More of Your Vacation

source.title: Royal Caribbean Says Sandals Deal Can Help It Win Half of Guests' Travel Spend

paragraphs: Royal Caribbean is one of the biggest cruise companies in the world. A cruise is a vacation on a large ship that stops at different places. On Tuesday, October 27, the company said its business did better than expected from July to September. But the bigger story is a plan to sell its guests more than a trip on a ship.

In those three months, Royal Caribbean earned $5.6 billion in revenue. That was 9% more than a year earlier. Its profit was $1.7 billion, up from $1.6 billion. The company carried 2.7 million guests, also 9% more than a year before. Guests also spent more aboard the ships. Revenue from what people buy aboard rose 14%.

The company said demand in Europe and the Caribbean was stronger than expected. Many people booked their trips late, and that helped. Because of the strong results, Royal Caribbean raised its goal for the full year. It now expects earnings of between $17.85 and $17.95 for each share.

Royal Caribbean has many loyal customers. Close to half of its guests this year are expected to be people who have traveled with it before. These loyal guests are crucial to the company. But the company says it gets only 20% to 25% of the money its guests spend on vacations each year. In other words, most of their vacation money goes somewhere else.

That is where a new deal comes in. In September, Royal Caribbean agreed to buy a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts and Beaches Resorts. A stake is a part of a company that you own. Sandals and Beaches run resorts on tropical islands, where guests pay one price for the room, the food and the drinks.

Their portfolio has 18 resorts in the Caribbean, and three more are being built. The portfolio also includes over 1,000 acres of land that is not used yet. Those acres give the resorts plenty of room to grow.

The two groups of customers are similar. About 30% of Royal Caribbean guests also take vacations at resorts like these. A similar share of Sandals and Beaches guests also go on cruises. With the deal, the company wants its share of each guest's vacation money to grow to roughly 50%. In business, people call this a bigger share of the customer's wallet. Royal Caribbean wants to be in that wallet for the cruise and for the tropical beach trip too.

The chief executive, Jason Liberty, said that a Royal Caribbean customer who travels with a rival brand is "a fail." According to Liberty, a connected loyalty program and great experiences should keep customers away from rival brands.

The deal is expected to close in early 2027, after the usual approvals. Liberty also said that bookings for 2027 are ahead of past years, at higher prices. These numbers demonstrate strong demand. The plan highlights a simple idea for travel companies: keep the same guests, and sell them more kinds of vacations.
